title: Spec-driven Development

body.text: Instead of giving commands one at a time, write a
spec — a document describing what the feature must do and what conditions apply
— then have Codex implement the whole thing per the spec. The result is more on-target and easier to verify.

example: "Spec: a coupon system — usable once per user, expires on a set date, can't combine with other promos, log every use"

title: Write a spec the AI can read

body.text: A spec the AI works well from needs
measurable behavior + input/output examples + exceptions (edge cases)
— if you haven't covered all the edge cases, ask the AI to point out which cases the spec doesn't yet cover.

example: "Read this spec and ask any unclear questions before writing code, e.g. coupons expire at midnight in which time zone?"

options.text: Write a doc of the desired behavior first, then have the AI implement it
Write code first, then figure out what it does

question: What must a good spec have?

options.text: Measurable behavior, examples, and edge cases

question: If you worry the spec isn't complete, what should you do?

options.text: Have the AI ask questions to find ambiguities before coding
Just start coding and fix it later

question: How do you do spec-driven development?

options.text: Write a clear spec for the AI to read and follow

question: What's the benefit of writing a spec for the AI?

options.text: Reduces misunderstandings and delivers on-target work
